title: Agentic AI Systems
summary: LLM agents that plan and act: a loop of reason → call tool → observe, with durable state, memory, sandboxed tools, budgets and human approval — built so long-running, multi-step work is reliable, observable and safe.

blocks.text: Framing: design a platform that runs AI agents for users — e.g. a support agent that reads tickets, queries internal systems, issues refunds within limits, and escalates to humans.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Agents take a goal, plan steps, call tools (APIs, DB queries, code), and return results
Long-running tasks (minutes to hours) that survive restarts; pause for human approval
Short-term (conversation) and long-term memory (user facts, past cases)
Safety: no unauthorized actions; every action auditable
Bounded cost and steps per task; observability of every step

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Each task is a multi-step loop, so cost and latency multiply by step count. The platform must checkpoint state between steps and cap steps, tokens and money per task.

items: **ReAct:** interleave reasoning and tool calls. **Plan-and-execute:** plan first, execute steps, re-plan on failure.
**Reflection / critic:** a reviewer step checks output before acting or finishing.
Structured tool calling (JSON schema arguments) instead of parsing free text.

blocks.caption: Durable orchestrator drives the loop; tools run in a sandbox behind a policy gate

sections.title: Deep dive: durable execution and state

items: Run agents on a durable workflow engine (Temporal, Step Functions, LangGraph with a Postgres checkpointer): each step is persisted so a crash resumes mid-task.
Tool calls carry idempotency keys so retries after a crash don't refund twice.
Long waits (human approval, webhook) suspend the workflow without holding a worker.
Context management: summarize or trim old steps; keep tool outputs as references (IDs/URLs) rather than pasting huge payloads into the prompt.

head: Memory
What
Store
rows: Vector store + metadata, retrieved by similarity
Stable facts about the user or org

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: Memory writes are a security surface: an injected instruction saved to memory can poison future tasks. Validate and scope what gets stored.

sections.title: Deep dive: tools, permissions and sandboxing

items: Tool registry with JSON schemas, descriptions, owner, scopes and risk level.
Agents act with the **user's** delegated permissions (OAuth scopes), never a super-user service account.
High-risk actions (payments, deletes, sending emails) require human approval or hard limits (refund ≤ ₹2,000).
Code execution and browsing in isolated sandboxes (gVisor/Firecracker containers), no network by default, CPU/time limits.
Treat all tool output as untrusted data: it may contain prompt injection; never let it change permissions.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The model proposes actions; a deterministic policy layer decides whether they run. Permissions, limits and approvals live outside the model.

head: Pattern
How
When
rows: A coordinator delegates to specialist agents
Planner writes steps, executors do them
Agents hand control to each other

blocks.text: More agents mean more tokens and more failure points; add them only when one agent with good tools can't do the job.

items: Trace every run: prompts, tool calls, arguments, outputs, latency, tokens, cost (LangSmith, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions).
Offline evals on datasets of tasks: success rate, steps taken, cost, policy violations; regression tests before shipping prompt/model changes.
Online: sample traces for LLM-as-judge scoring, user feedback, escalation rate.
Guard metrics: loops detected, budget exhaustion, approval rejections.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Max steps, token and money budgets, loop detection
Schema validation, dry-run, confirmation for risky tools
Least privilege, output isolation, egress allowlists
Fallback models, queue with retries, pause and resume

items.title: HLD
items.text: Queue → orchestrator → LLM gateway + tool sandbox; state, memory, traces.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Durable state, tool permissions, memory, evals.

items.q: How do you stop an agent from running forever?
items.a: Step, token, wall-clock and money budgets enforced by the orchestrator, plus repetition detection; on exhaustion, summarize and escalate.

items.q: How do you test an agent?
items.a: Scenario datasets with mocked tools, assert outcomes and forbidden actions; replay production traces; track success rate per release.
As the standard interface for exposing tools and data to agents — see the next case study.

items: Loop: decide → act → observe → checkpoint.
Durable execution + idempotent tools.
Policy layer outside the model; user-scoped permissions.
Sandbox code/browse tools; treat tool output as untrusted.
Budgets on steps, tokens, money.
Trace and evaluate every run.
